97	### Decision D1
98	- Basis: R2
99	R2 as drafted asked that a comment written in inline code keep its text. Telling inline code from a real comment is the kind of Markdown reading that took the origin spec four rounds to make fail-closed; instead, any comment marker inside the accepted limits section refuses the section whole, and the ready check says so. A comment outside the section, including one that holds an example section, is still stripped and not read. A marker written in inline code (an odd number of backticks before it on its line) opens no comment, as Markdown shows it as text; the spec's own ready check found that its R2, which names the marker, was taken for an unterminated comment.
